title: Where the lake once spilled over
text: A narrow gorge southeast of China Lake once afforded the lowest exit for surface drainage from Indian Wells Valley. It is now filled with windblown sand and is part of the Salt Wells Valley drainage, and the divide on it has a surface altitude of 2,190 feet. A granite ridge at an altitude of about 2,400 feet marks the apparent site of rapids of another outlet, used when the level of a perennial lake was above 2,400 feet.
